title: Representing a graph: adjacency lists
summary: Each vertex keeps a linked list of its neighbours, so memory grows with the number of edges.

checkpoints.text: An array of 4 list heads, one per vertex. Edge 0–1 is added to vertex 0's list as a node holding 1.
Undirected again: the same edge goes into vertex 1's list too, as a node holding 0.
Three edges, six nodes. Each new neighbour was inserted at the front of its list, so vertex 0's list reads 2 then 1.
Listing a vertex's neighbours walks only its own list: no empty cells to skip, unlike a matrix row.
Adjacency lists use memory for V heads plus one node per edge end, much less than V² for a sparse graph. The matrix answers "is u connected to v?" faster.
